newsitem.title: USA: GOLF-NORMAN VISITS CLINTON; NO INJURIES REPORTED.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-NORMAN VISITS CLINTON; NO INJURIES REPORTED.

text.p: In a reverse reprise of one of the most famous house visits in recent history, Greg Norman visited the White House this week -- three months after U.S. President Bill Clinton injured his knee in a fall at the golfer's home.

Norman, who has been extremely tight-lipped about the details of the president's fall, was also reticent about his Monday visit with Clinton, although he did offer some comments about the day and the president.

"I thought it was great. My children are U.S. citizens. I thought it would be wonderful for them to go to the White House," the Australian golfer said on Tuesday as he prepared for the U.S. Open at Congressional Country Club -- just 15 miles (24 km) from the Oval Office.
"It was one of those days that I thought was a very special day for my family."
Norman also offered an update on Clinton's physical condition and his golf game.
"It was good to see the president up and around. He is starting to chip and pitch the ball -- and he's walking around without any problems.

Clinton, an avid golfer, injured a tendon in his knee when he fell at Norman's home in Hobe Sound, Florida, and he was forced to spend some time in a wheelchair and then weeks more on crutches while the knee healed.
"He's lost 30 pounds (14 kg). He feels great. He thanks me for it -- the fact he's lost 30 pounds," Norman said.
Norman did not say how the junk-food-loving president, who usually jogs daily to control his weight, managed to lose so many pounds while remaining so sedate.
"A couple of his staff came up to me and said: 'That's the best thing that ever happened to him. Don't worry about it because it slowed him down for a couple of months.'"
The inactivity also made the president anxious to get back on the golf course, Norman said.
"He was very upbeat and excited about getting back and playing again."
